steps.title: Import React, createContext, useContext, and useState
steps.instruction: Import React, createContext, useContext, and useState from 'react'
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary React APIs for creating and using context.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing multiple items from a module
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React, createContext, useContext, and useState from 'react'
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary React APIs are imported and available for use in the Auth Context implementation.
successCriteria: React, createContext, useContext, and useState are imported from 'react'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported all the necessary React APIs for working with context.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure to import all four items: React, createContext, useContext, and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Please import React, createContext, useContext, and useState from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the AuthContext
steps.instruction: Create an AuthContext using React.createContext() and export it as a named export.
steps.hint: Use the createContext function you imported to create a new context object. Name it AuthContext and export it.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React, createContext, useContext, and useState from 'react'

// Create the AuthContext here
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have an AuthContext object created and exported, ready to be used by other components.
successCriteria: AuthContext is created using React.createContext() and exported as a named export.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the AuthContext. This context will hold the authentication state and functions for your app.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using React.createContext() and exporting the AuthContext as a named export.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create an AuthContext using React.createContext() and export it.

steps.title: Create the AuthProvider component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named AuthProvider that takes children as props and returns them wrapped in AuthContext.Provider.
steps.hint: Define a component that accepts children and returns <AuthContext.Provider value={null}>{children}</AuthContext.Provider>.
steps.expectedOutcome: An AuthProvider component is defined that returns AuthContext.Provider wrapping children.
successCriteria: AuthProvider is a functional component that accepts children and returns AuthContext.Provider with a placeholder value prop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the AuthProvider component that will wrap your app and provide authentication state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure AuthProvider is a function that takes children and returns AuthContext.Provider with a value prop (even if null for now).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named AuthProvider that returns AuthContext.Provider wrapping children.

steps.title: Initialize authentication state in AuthProvider
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthProvider component, add a useState hook to manage an isAuthenticated state variable, initializing it to false.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Declare it inside the component body.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthProvider component now has a state variable isAuthenticated initialized to false.
successCriteria: The useState hook is declared inside AuthProvider with isAuthenticated and setIsAuthenticated, initialized to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've initialized the authentication state. The isAuthenticated variable will track whether a user is logged in.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with isAuthenticated and setIsAuthenticated, initialized to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to add a useState hook inside AuthProvider to manage isAuthenticated state.

steps.title: Create login handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthProvider component, create a function named login that sets the isAuthenticated state to true.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls the setter function from useState with the value true.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthProvider component now contains a login function that will update the authentication state.
successCriteria: A function named login is defined inside AuthProvider and it calls setIsAuthenticated(true).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the login handler function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a function named login that calls setIsAuthenticated(true).
steps.feedbackWrong: The login function is missing or doesn't properly set isAuthenticated to true.

steps.title: Create logout handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your AuthProvider component, create a function named handleLogout that sets isAuthenticated to false.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls setIsAuthenticated with false. This function will be used later to log out the user.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthProvider component now contains a handleLogout function that updates the authentication state.
successCriteria: A function named handleLogout is defined inside AuthProvider and calls setIsAuthenticated(false).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the logout handler function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a function named handleLogout that sets isAuthenticated to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The logout handler function is missing or incorrect. Create a function named handleLogout that calls setIsAuthenticated(false).

steps.title: Set up AuthProvider return structure
steps.instruction: In the AuthProvider component's return statement, pass the authentication state and handler functions as the value prop to AuthContext.Provider.
steps.hint: The value prop should be an object containing isAuthenticated, login, and logout.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthProvider component now provides authentication state and handlers to its children via context.
successCriteria: The AuthContext.Provider's value prop contains an object with isAuthenticated, login, and logout.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The AuthProvider now passes the authentication state and handlers through context, making them available to any child component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the value prop includes all three items: isAuthenticated, login, and logout.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AuthProvider's return structure is incomplete. The value prop should contain the authentication state and handler functions.

steps.title: Create useAuth custom hook
steps.instruction: Define a custom hook named useAuth that returns the value from useContext(AuthContext).
steps.hint: Create a function that calls useContext with AuthContext as its argument and returns the result.
steps.expectedOutcome: A custom hook named useAuth is created, which will allow components to easily access the authentication context.
successCriteria: The useAuth function is defined and returns the result of useContext(AuthContext).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the useAuth custom hook. This will make it easy for components to consume the authentication context.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your useAuth function calls useContext with AuthContext and returns the result.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useAuth hook isn't quite right. Remember to define a function named useAuth that returns useContext(AuthContext).

steps.title: Create a LoginButton component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named LoginButton that uses the useAuth hook.
steps.hint: Define a new component that calls useAuth to get the auth context values.
steps.expectedOutcome: A LoginButton component is defined that will later use the auth context.
successCriteria: The LoginButton component is created and uses the useAuth hook.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the LoginButton component and used the useAuth hook.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it uses the useAuth hook.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component is missing or doesn't use the useAuth hook.

steps.title: Add login button and wire onClick to login handler
steps.instruction: Inside the LoginButton component, add a button element with the text 'Log In' and wire its onClick event to call the login function from the AuthContext.
steps.hint: Use the useAuth hook to access the login function from context, then create a button with onClick={login}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The LoginButton component will render a button that triggers the login function when clicked.
successCriteria: LoginButton component contains a button element with text 'Log In' and onClick={login}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a login button that uses the context login function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the login function from context and wiring it to the button's onClick.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't properly connected to the login function. Check that you're using the login function from context and the onClick attribute.

steps.title: Add logout button and wire onClick to logout handler
steps.instruction: In the LoginButton component, add a logout button element that calls the logout function from context when clicked.
steps.hint: Add a second button element with an onClick handler that calls logout. Place it after the existing login button.
steps.expectedOutcome: The LoginButton component will have two buttons: one for login and one for logout, both wired to their respective context handlers.
successCriteria: A logout button element is added to the LoginButton component with an onClick handler that calls the logout function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a logout button that will trigger the logout function when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a logout button, but make sure it has an onClick handler that calls the logout function from context.
steps.feedbackWrong: The logout button is missing or not properly wired. Add a button element with onClick={logout} inside the LoginButton component.

steps.title: Display authentication status in LoginButton
steps.instruction: Inside the LoginButton component, display the current isAuthenticated value from context by using the useAuth hook.
steps.hint: Call useAuth() to get the authentication context, then display the isAuthenticated value in your JSX.
steps.expectedOutcome: The LoginButton component will show the current authentication status from context.
successCriteria: LoginButton uses useAuth to get isAuthenticated and displays it in the UI.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully displayed the authentication status in the LoginButton component using context.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling useAuth() and displaying the isAuthenticated value in your JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The LoginButton component doesn't yet display the authentication status. Remember to use the useAuth hook to access the context value.
